tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your Monday September 21st morning game plan.

The macro setup is genuinely confusing. Futures are rallying — S&P up about 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 110 basis points, Russell up 47 basis points — but almost every piece of weekend news flow was net negative. Asia closed broadly higher, Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with strength in industrials, tech, and banks, and Treasuries have a mild bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

So why are stocks rallying? The answer appears to be the UN General Assembly, which runs this week in New York. Trump signaled he would be open to meeting with Iran's president, who is expected to attend. Markets are betting that even a tiny de-escalation in Middle East tensions could crack oil prices lower — and right now, nearly every macro problem can be traced back to oil. Lower oil means lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, better margins, and improved consumer confidence. That is the entire bull thesis in a single sentence. Brent is already sliding 170 basis points this morning to around 102 dollars a barrel.

But the bears have plenty of ammunition. The Houthis launched a major missile and drone attack on Saudi Arabia over the weekend. Ukraine hit Russia with its largest drone strike of the war. And a flood of AI headlines hit after Friday's close — Anthropic's IPO has been delayed, the company's 2027 revenue projections disappointed, OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of roughly 280 billion dollars from 2026 through 2030, and Oracle's Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico is facing debt offloading problems. That is a serious cluster of negative AI infrastructure news. On the monetary policy front, global central banks remain firmly hawkish — the Fed, ECB, and Bank of Japan all hiked this month, and markets are pricing more than 50 percent odds of additional increases in October and November from multiple central banks. Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari both warned over the weekend that inflation is broad-based, not just oil-driven.

On the company side, Disney's parks business is outperforming as the company uses price promotions and package deals to drive attendance while peers are struggling with traffic headwinds — that is a relative positive for Disney. Novo Nordisk is getting hit in Europe after failing to provide granular financial targets at its analyst day, disappointing investors despite touting future blockbuster drug launches. Oracle faces fresh pressure after that Financial Times piece on stalled debt tied to its New Mexico data center. And Paramount is in advanced settlement talks with California over the Warner merger, potentially agreeing to preserve CNN's editorial independence and divest Comedy Central, though other state attorneys general are not yet aligned.

The week's big macro catalysts are the US flash PMIs Wednesday morning and the Trump-Xi summit Thursday. On the earnings front: AutoZone reports Tuesday morning, Cintas, General Mills, and Paychex Wednesday morning, Darden and SNX Thursday morning, and Costco Thursday night.

The directional read: this is a show-me moment. The rally makes sense only if the UN General Assembly produces at least a whisper of diplomatic progress on Iran. If there is no signal by mid-week, this morning's strength could fade quickly. Watch oil — it is the single most important variable in the market right now. Stay nimble.
